Cc: billing@brightwave.ai
Date: 2026-10-28T08:45:00Z
Subject: Orphaned ingest events causing October spike

Hi Vanessa —

Over the last 36 hours we've seen a ~42% jump in token consumption billed to our account (BrightWave Labs) that we can't reconcile in our dashboards. The traffic pattern looks like short-lived bursts (~10–60s) producing lots of small sessions; they don't match our normal production traffic.

Can Redwood pull the raw ingest rows or provide example event samples for the spike window (UTC Oct 27 22:00 — Oct 28 06:00)? We suspect some staging workers were misconfigured and pushed via the production API key. If that's the case we will ask for a billing credit.

Attaching the CSV export we pulled from our side (we'll send full logs if you can give a presigned S3).

Thanks —
Asha Reddy
Head of Engineering Ops
BrightWave Labs

Hi Asha — thanks for the heads up and the export. We've flagged this to billing and engineering; copied Ben and Karthik.

A few quick asks so we can triage and scope a provisional credit:
- Can you confirm which API key(s) were used for the traffic in your CSV (production vs staging)?
- Are the CID/session IDs consistent across the rows or do they look like ephemeral test runs?
- Do you want a provisional credit while we audit, or do you prefer we finish the root-cause first and then propose adjustments?

Ben: can you pull the token-by-session counts for BrightWave for Oct 27–28 (UTC) and compare to the same window last week? Karthik: can you start with raw ingest samples and the service-side audit logs for the same time window. If we find staging-origin traffic, we'll recommend a credit and outline VAT handling (EU).

I'll coordinate the evidence exchange; if you can share a presigned S3 link to the full log bundle that will speed things up.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Asha / Vanessa —

I pulled the billing shard for BrightWave and compared token counts. Summary (preliminary):
- Oct 27 00:00–Oct 28 23:59 UTC: +41.9% tokens vs prior 48-hour baseline.
- The increase is concentrated in short sessions (median 38 tokens/session) and a large number of unique request IDs that don't match longer-running production sessions.

Quick clarifying Qs:
1) Do you use multiple API keys for different environments? If yes, send the key IDs.
2) Do you want us to hold any invoice adjustments until legal signs off, or proceed with a provisional credit now and reconcile later?

If the origin is confirmed as non-production, provisional credits for usage are our standard handling; VAT treatment depends on whether BrightWave wants a fiscal credit line on the invoice or a gross refund. If you prefer fiscal credit on the next invoice we can prepare the amended charge with VAT annotation.

Attaching a short CSV with session-level token counts and a suggested provisional credit range (see provisional-credit-estimate.xlsx).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Billing Operations — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, Asha Reddy <asha@brightwave.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T13:54:00Z
Subject: Re: Orphaned ingest events causing October spike

Thanks for the context — dug into the service logs and sample exports. TL;DR: we see a timestamp drift on a small set of collectors that caused several staging jobs to be accepted as production for ~2.5 hours. Evidence below.

What I pulled:
- Attached: audit-log-snippet.txt (service-side accept events), ingest-sample-exports.csv (10 sample requests).
- Investigator notes: extractor-42 (EU region) had its local clock off by +1 hour starting at 2026-10-27T21:58:12Z; a cron job on the staging fleet was using the production API key and replayed a backlog. The collector accepted the requests because auth matched; the telemetry shows short-lived request bursts with ephemeral session ids (prefix "stg-").

Sample lines from audit-log-snippet.txt (redacted):
2026-10-27T22:05:03Z accept request_id=stg-9f3a token_count=46 api_key=pk_live_*** collector=extractor-42 zone=eu
2026-10-27T22:05:04Z accept request_id=stg-9f3b token_count=12 api_key=pk_live_*** collector=extractor-42 zone=eu

Counts:
- Total affected requests accepted: 127,432 requests
- Total token delta attributable to these requests: ~3.1M tokens (estimated)

Proposal for remediation and next steps:
1) We recommend a provisional credit equal to the token delta converted at your current rate: provisional credit = 3.1M tokens * your per-token rate (we calculated an estimated gross credit in provisional-credit-estimate.xlsx and included VAT scenarios).
2) We'll issue a credit memo and can either: (a) apply as a fiscal credit to your next invoice (annotated for VAT), or (b) issue a refund if you prefer a cash return.
3) We'll rotate the affected API key and push a tagging guard to prevent staging agents from using production keys.

Ben — can you prepare the credit memo draft? Asha — if you approve the provisional credit we can move to preparing the amended invoice and DocuSign amendment for the mid-cycle change.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer — Serving Runtime
From: Asha Reddy <asha@brightwave.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-30T16:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Orphaned ingest events causing October spike

Thanks all — this aligns with our internal findings. Confirming: the staging cron accidentally replayed a backlog to production due to a config error; request ids have the "stg-" prefix and we can produce the full staging log bundle.

We accept Redwood's proposed provisional credit for the 3.1M-token delta, applied as a fiscal credit on our next invoice with VAT annotation (EU). Please:
- Ben: draft the credit memo / amended invoice and include the VAT line (we're in Ireland; VAT reverse-charge applies but we need the annotation).
- Vanessa: please include an S3 presigned link for the full raw logs so our auditors can download evidence.
- Karthik: please rotate the API key and confirm the tagging guard rollout ETA.

We'll sign the DocuSign amendment for the invoice once Ben shares it. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Asha
